Here's why: If Carol picked 28 and her mom picked 17, the total would be 45, and there would still be 7 bad carrots. But if Carol picked 30 and her mom picked 15, the total would also be 45, and there would be 7 bad carrots. But if Carol picked 29 and her mom picked 17, the total would be 46 and there would be 8 bad carrots. To get a different number of bad carrots, you have to have a different total number of carrots. And if you change either 29 or 16 to a number that is 1 higher or 1 lower than 29 or 16, the total number of carrots will be the same. You could change 29 to 31 or 28, and change 16 to 15 or 17. Changing 29 to 31 will make the total 47. Changing 29 to 28 will make the total 44. Changing 16 to 15 will make the total 44. Changing 16 to 17 will make the total 46. So only the number 7 will work.
The answer is \boxed{7}. -- Bryan Brock, grade 6

To find out how many weeks that actually amounts to, we need to determine what a dollar per week amount to his total income of $40.  If he earns $40, a dollar is equal to $40/40 = $1.  Now if the above equation is simplified and $40 is divided by $1, we get
$35 ÷ $1 = 35
You answer is $$\boxed{35}$$.

Expository Text features:
– it aims to describe, explain, or summarize a topic

– it may include definitions, examples, and explanations
– it is often written in a neutral tone, but can also be formal or informal depending on the context
Narrative Text features:
– it aims to tell a story or convey a message
– it uses descriptive language and structures the story in a logical and coherent sequence
– it often includes character development, plot twists, and conflict resolution
– it can be written in first person or third person, and can be formal or informal
Persuasive Text features:

– uses objective language
– presents information in a clear and concise manner

– can be formal or academic in tone
Narrative Text characteristics:
– uses descriptive and imaginative language
– tells a story or conveys a message
– often includes character development, plot twists, and conflict resolution
– can be formal or informal in tone
Persuasive Text characteristics:
– uses persuasive language and rhetorical devices
– aims to convince or persuade the reader to adopt a particular point of view or take a particular action
